Question B-007-002-006.

Why the correct answer is right: Ionization is generally strongest around midday because solar radiation is then most direct on the daylight side of the path.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Dawn": Dawn follows a night of recombination, so ionization is not at its maximum then.
- sourceIndex 2: "Midnight": Midnight has no direct sunlight on that region, so ionization usually has decreased rather than peaked.
- sourceIndex 3: "Dusk": Dusk comes after solar input is declining; it is not the normal daily maximum.
